clue.text: Ill-fated king removed and arraigned

indicators.note: removed tells us the king's letter is taken out of the ill-fated word

parts.note: ill-fated means doomed, under a curse
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A doomed monarch is deposed and put on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' takes R out of ACCURSED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be arraigned is to be formally charged in court with a crime.

clue.text: Godless robbery in heartless story

indicators.note: in puts the robbery inside the shortened storey
heartless removes the middle letter of the word for story

parts.note: an attic is the top storey of a house
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: An irreligious crime inside a soulless tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' stands for storey, a floor of a house; 'heartless' drops its middle letter, leaving ATIC, and 'in' puts the robbery inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Denying the existence of any deity.

clue.text: His first letter is top of the column

definitions.meaning: a name's opening letter is written in upper case
the decorated head of an architectural pillar

explanation.definitionFit: An upper-case letter and the crowning part of a pillar share one name.

clue.text: Whop with stick, perhaps, to get cattle moving

definitions.text: Whop with stick, perhaps, to get cattle moving

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words whop and stick may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A drover hits with a stick to move the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges WHOP and STICK; the whole clue describes the herdsman's lash.
explanation.definitionFit: A drover's long lash on a short handle, used to drive livestock.

clue.text: Make tracks for the boat

parts.note: to make is to do
RY is short for railway, a set of tracks

explanation.surface: Hurry off to catch the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make tracks' reads as one idiom for leaving; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flat-bottomed rowing craft.

clue.text: Drinker who gives a pourboire — about a pound

indicators.note: about means the tipper's letters go around the pound sign

parts.note: a pourboire is French for a tip, so one who gives it is a tipper
L is the abbreviation for pound (Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A drinker who leaves a gratuity of around a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside TIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual drinker of alcohol, especially one who sips often, is called this.

clue.text: Elephant less cramped, we hear, in Alabama

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is spoken and matched by sound

parts.note: a tusker is an elephant, and less cramped is looser

explanation.surface: An elephant given more room in a southern US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says 'tusker looser' said aloud matches the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the US state, home of its university.

clue.text: Direct one into parking place

indicators.note: into puts the one inside the parking place

parts.note: P for parking plus lot, a place
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Guide someone into a car-park space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts I inside P LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer or guide, as a navigator does a ship.

clue.text: Brown coal left on fire

indicators.note: on means the left letter is placed before the fire word in a down clue

parts.note: to fire is to ignite, set alight

explanation.surface: Coal left burning in the grate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue sets L above IGNITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, low-grade fuel is the technical name for this kind of coal.

clue.text: Precocious article by artist

indicators.note: by means the article sits next to the artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An early piece written by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets THE beside RA.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning early or ripening early.

clue.text: He might take a sort of bath by the river

definitions.text: He might take a sort of bath by the river

parts.note: a hip bath is a small bath you sit in up to the hips
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Someone who likes bathing beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the river horse, which wallows in rivers; 'by' sets the river after the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: The African river horse spends its days submerged in rivers and mud wallows.

clue.text: Lose no time with answer to clue needing little brilliance

parts.note: to lose no time is to hurry or rush
in crosswords a light is an answer entered in the grid

explanation.surface: Hurrying to solve a clue that needs no great cleverness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little brilliance' reads as a lack of cleverness, but it means feeble illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle made by dipping a reed's pith in tallow gave only a dim glow.

clue.text: New pupils at school get consumption

definitions.meaning: the year's new admissions to a school
the amount of food or drink taken in

explanation.definitionFit: A school's yearly admissions and the quantity a body takes in share one word for what comes in.

clue.text: The cellar is stocked from this place of unremitting toil

definitions.text: The cellar is stocked from this
definitions.meaning: a salt cellar, the little table pot, is filled from underground workings

explanation.definitionFit: Underground workings for rock condiment, and figuratively any scene of endless drudgery.

clue.text: Cut into a steak initially, and dined in state

indicators.note: into means the cut goes inside the other letters
initially means only the first letter of steak is used

parts.note: dined means ate
to cut is to sever

explanation.surface: Slicing a steak and eating it grandly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' sends the cut between AS and the dining word. 'state' looks like a noun but is the verb, to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare or affirm solemnly.

clue.text: Heel over root of hydrangea in well-dug soil

parts.note: a ship heels over when it leans, or tilts

indicators.note: the root of a word is its start, so its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A gardener's shrub leaning over in freshly worked ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The cultivated, crumbly state of tilled ground is a gardening term.

clue.text: Poor Hilary perhaps has but a little time

parts.note: poor in the sense of lacking, short of
Hilary is the Oxford University and law-court term running from January to Easter

explanation.surface: Someone called Hilary has little time left.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary looks like a person's name; it is a British university and legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting only a brief period, not long-lasting.

clue.text: What you get when you go in the dining car — and its cost?

definitions.text: What you get when you go in the dining car — and its cost?

parts.words: What you get when you go in the dining car — and its cost?
parts.note: the food served on a railway journey, and also the ticket price for travelling

explanation.definitionFit: Railway catering and the price of a ticket share one phrase.

clue.text: Tapestry may well be so antique

definitions.meaning: old fabric is often eaten by insect larvae

explanation.definitionFit: Fabric damaged by larvae, and figuratively worn out or antiquated.

clue.text: Inexpensive cape is poor quality

parts.note: inexpensive means cheap
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A low-priced cloak turns out to be shoddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a garment; it is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shoddy or tawdry, of low worth.

clue.text: This waterfall shows the pull of a big attraction

definitions.text: This waterfall shows the pull of a big attraction

parts.words: This waterfall shows the pull of a big attraction
parts.note: the sea falls back under the moon's gravity, a fall of water

explanation.definitionFit: The receding tide is drawn by the moon's gravitational force.

clue.text: Doctor leaving in the midst of general anxiety

indicators.note: leaving means the doctor's letters go out of the other word

parts.note: in the midst of means among, or amongst
MO is a medical officer, a military doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor walks out amid widespread worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes MO out of AMONGST; 'in the midst of' looks like a selection signal but gives a whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: A diffuse dread or unease, borrowed from German, is a generalised worry.

clue.text: Screened and questioned

definitions.meaning: fitted with a grille, a screen of bars

explanation.definitionFit: Covered with a barred screen, and interrogated hard.

clue.text: Lost one's stripes? Certainly refused admission

definitions.meaning: read as ..., stripped of one's bars or stripes

explanation.definitionFit: Being excluded from entry, and humorously having one's bars removed.

clue.text: Some undiscovered jockey may work here

indicators.note: some means only part of the word undiscovered is used

explanation.surface: An unknown rider might ride here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockey' is a disc jockey, not a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub where a record-playing DJ works.

clue.text: Enlarges papers

definitions.meaning: widens a hole with a tool

explanation.definitionFit: Widening a bore with a tool, and large quantities of writing sheets.

clue.text: Bowling team are in lawful possession of the ball

definitions.text: in lawful possession of the ball

parts.note: in cricket the bowler currently bowling is said to be on
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A cricket fielding team claiming the ball legally.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler who is bowling is 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and rugby a player in a legal position to play the ball is not offside.

clue.text: Shooters turn up well protected from the cold

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue reads the word for shooters from the bottom

parts.note: shooters is slang for guns

explanation.surface: Hunters arrive warmly wrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' in a down clue reverses GUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cosy, sheltered spot is one that keeps out draughts and chill.

clue.text: Prays in an unusual posture to make a story

indicators.note: an unusual posture rearranges the words prays in an

explanation.surface: Someone kneels oddly to pray and invents a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual posture' rearranges PRAYSINAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell a tall tale or long story is a sailors' idiom.

clue.text: Many hold the pound share

indicators.note: hold means the word for many contains the pound sign

parts.note: many means a lot
L is the abbreviation for pound (Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Many people keep a share of the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' puts L inside A LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To share out is to distribute or apportion.

clue.text: Manage to write poem in Old English

indicators.note: in places the verse inside the abbreviation

parts.note: to verse is to write poetry

explanation.surface: Trying to compose verse in Anglo-Saxon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to write poem' is a verb phrase: verse can mean to compose poetry; 'in' places it inside the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or direct work.

clue.text: Undergo reform for reward

indicators.note: reform here means the word undergo is formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A prisoner reforms to earn a reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges UNDERGO.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a recompense or prize.
